Cuts a slow fuzz-determinism check from tens of minutes to a fraction of that for large corpora.

result.summary: This PR optimizes contrib/devtools/deterministic-fuzz-coverage by comparing merged .profdata files before rendering full llvm-cov show reports. Because identical profdata implies identical coverage output, the expensive llvm-cov rendering step is skipped entirely for the common case where fuzz coverage is deterministic, falling back to the old render-and-diff behavior only when profdata differs. The pass/fail result is unchanged.
result.problem: The tool previously rendered a full llvm-cov show report for every fuzz input on both runs and diffed them, even though almost all inputs produce deterministic coverage, wasting the most expensive step of the process. Contributors running this tool (e.g. during PR review of #35809) experienced multi-hour runs on large corpora like process_message.

resolved_concerns: maflcko's nit to de-duplicate check_diff/run_profile/render_cov was partially addressed; author kept profdata_eq separate for readability, no further pushback.

jeanpablojp's concern that a build missing -fcoverage-mapping would now pass silently was addressed by maflcko's rationale that this is a dev-only script and the logic should not be complicated for misconfigured builds; jeanpablojp did not push back.

result.card: This PR optimizes the contrib/devtools/deterministic-fuzz-coverage Rust tool by comparing merged .profdata files before falling back to the expensive llvm-cov show rendering step, skipping rendering entirely when profdata is identical (a sufficient condition for deterministic coverage). It solves a real pain point for contributors: jeanpablojp independently reproduced the benchmark and found process_message runtime dropping from 1h50m to 26 minutes with identical pass/fail results. The PR has a tested ACK and an approval, with one style nit partially addressed and one edge-case concern explicitly resolved by a maintainer as out of scope. It is Ready for merge-oriented review, with Strong agreement, and is a niche developer-tool improvement (P3 in tools) rather than a broadly user-facing change. It conflicts with the same author's open PR #35809 which should be considered for merge ordering.
